sections.content: How many people are "food, drink and tobacco process operatives"?

146,535 people

were counted on the census as "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Food, drink and tobacco process operatives set, operate and attend machinery to bake, freeze, heat, crush, mix, blend and otherwise process foodstuffs, beverages and tobacco leaves.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "food, drink and tobacco process operatives", 12.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" included:

  • stock control clerks and assistants
  • vehicle paint technicians
  • rail travel assistants

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" there were more men than women (62.1% compared with 37.9%).

This means "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 62.1% and women made up 37.9% of "food, drink and tobacco process operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" included:

  • inspectors of standards and regulations
  • protective service associate professionals (other)
  • glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "food, drink and tobacco process operatives" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "food, drink and tobacco process operatives", 7.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (83.2% compared with 16.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.6%) than self-employed (3.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the East Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leicester, this is in the same region of the East Midlands.
